inconsistencies: #29247 (OP_CAT) and #36122 (BIP460 CISA) are the same kind of item for this category: consensus soft-fork reference implementations whose only mempool content is standardness/discouragement policy that cannot be settled until the consensus direction is. They are held at the same band; neither should displace the two P2 bug fixes, and #29247 is placed first of the two only because it is a narrower, self-contained change while #36122 is explicitly an experimental draft not offered for merge.

#29843 (-acceptnonstdtxn relaxing non-standard script execution on test nets) is the policy-side enabler for exercising exactly the unactivated-opcode spends that #29247 and #36122 introduce; if reviewers take up the soft-fork drafts, #29843 is the one to review first since it removes the testnet mempool friction those proposals otherwise hit.

#35882 and #35923 are both narrow, test-only or accounting-only items with no user-visible consequence; they sit together at the bottom and neither has a claim over the P3 work despite #35923 being labelled a bug fix (~80 bytes per unbroadcast tx).

#35286 (testsubmitpackage) and #36214 (cluster limits during reorgs) both touch the package/cluster mempool work but do not overlap: #35286 exposes a dry-run RPC for wallets, #36214 only adds regression coverage for existing trimming logic. No duplication, no ordering dependency.
result.notes: No bands were changed from the individual assessments; the list already separates cleanly into two genuine mempool-behaviour fixes (fee estimation fallback, BIP68 lockpoint recalculation on reorg), a middle tier of policy/RPC/test work with a clear use case, and two marginal items. The soft-fork reference implementations (#29247, #36122) are consensus-first work that only grazes this category, so they are ranked at the tail of P3 rather than raised on novelty; #36214 is lifted within P3 because cluster mempool is a category-defining project and the test guards its trimming behaviour under reorg.
